transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Lately I feel drained all the time, like I don’t have the energy to get through my workday or even enjoy fishing on the weekends. It just feels like I'm running on empty constantly, and I can't seem to shake it.
How long have you been feeling this way, and has this happened before as a separate episode, or did it start after a particular stressful event?

This current low mood has been hanging over me for about eleven months, though these cycles of feeling highly revved up for a week and then crashing have been happening off and on for about a year. They really came into focus over the last few months when my IT firm took on new contracts, and things completely bottomed out after I recently got a formal warning from my supervisor.

During these low periods, have you had any psychotic symptoms, like hearing or seeing things others don’t, or strongly believing something that others say isn’t true? If so, did those experiences happen only when your mood was very low?
No, I’ve never experienced anything like that. I’ve never seen or heard things that aren’t there, and I don't have any unusual beliefs that others find strange.

During those week-long times when you felt highly revved up, did you need much less sleep and feel unusually confident or energetic, talking more, having racing thoughts, or doing risky or impulsive things? Did those periods cause problems at work or with other people?

Yes, during those high times I only needed three or four hours of sleep but woke up totally wired, talking a mile a minute and staying up late buying expensive tech gear on my credit card. I got obsessed with overhauling systems and would get really snappy if anyone questioned my ideas. While my actual work write-up happened during my low phase, those high periods definitely strained things with my wife and raised some eyebrows at the office.

During those revved-up periods, did you ever become so impaired that you had to be hospitalized, missed work because of it, or did things that caused major consequences beyond arguments and overspending? Did anyone around you feel you were out of touch with reality during those times?

No, I never lost touch with reality or needed to be hospitalized, and I didn't actually miss any work during those high periods. The warning from my boss only happened later when I crashed into this low, drained phase and started making mistakes. When I was revved up, the main issues were just me getting really snappy with people who questioned me and overspending on my credit cards.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a bipolar course with distinct week-long elevated/activated periods marked by decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, increased goal-directed activity/obsessive projects, irritability, and overspending, followed by a current prolonged depressive episode with low mood, anergia, and loss of interest. There is clear history of hypomanic symptoms without psychosis, hospitalization, or severe impairment during the elevated periods, and no psychotic symptoms during depression. This is most consistent with bipolar affective disorder, current episode mild or moderate depression.
